In Madinah there were two boys from the Ansar, and each of them was named Mu'adh: Mu'adh ibn Amr and Mu'adh ibn Afra'.

They used to hear that Abu Jahl in Makkah insulted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tortured the weak Muslims, and this made them angry.

Then Quraysh set out with a big army against the Muslims, and Abu Jahl was in it.

The Muslims went out to meet them and camped at Badr. They had fewer men and fewer weapons. The two boys went out with them, each with his sword.

When the Muslims lined up in rows, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf stood in the row. He looked to his right and to his left, and found himself between two young boys.

He wished he were between two men stronger than them, who would stand by him if the fighting became hard.

One of them nudged him secretly and said, "Uncle, do you know Abu Jahl?"

He said, "Yes. What do you want with him, my nephew?"

He said, "I was told that he insults the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By the One in whose hand my soul is, if I see him, I will not leave him until whichever of us is meant to die first dies."

Abd al-Rahman was amazed at what the boy said.

Then the other boy nudged him from the other side and said the same thing as his friend, and neither of them had heard the other.

Soon Abd al-Rahman saw Abu Jahl moving among the people, with men around him guarding him.

He said to the two boys, "There he is — the man you asked me about."

The two boys rushed toward him. They were not stopped by how young they were, or by the men around him, or by the fact that he was the chief of Quraysh.

They struck him with their swords until they killed him.

Then they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him. He said, "Which of you killed him?" Each of them said, "I killed him."

He said, "Have you wiped your swords?" They said, "No." He looked at the two swords and said, "You both killed him."

Allah gave the Muslims victory that day, even though they were few.

﴿وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ وَأَنتُمْ أَذِلَّةٌ﴾

And Abd al-Rahman realized that the two boys he had wished were stronger had the strongest hearts of all.

Strength is not in being tall or old. It is in a heart that becomes angry for Allah's sake and steps forward when others hold back.

📖 Agreed upon (Al-Bukhari and Muslim).
